message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Use a PC build checklist or a site like PCPartPicker to avoid incompatibilities. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Place it at the bottom or top (depending on case). Secure with screws, route cables. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for everything else. | Align standoffs, screw in, then attach I/O shield. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | If cooler has pre‑applied paste, skip. Otherwise, apply a pea‑size amount. Attach cooler, secure. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Open slots, align notch, push until clicks. |
|10 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into slot, screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming. | Remove PCIe slot covers, insert card, secure with screws. |
|12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS for CPU, 6/8‑pin PCIe for GPU, SATA power for drives. |
|13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer. | SATA data cables for HDD/SSD, M.2 data is built‑in. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Keeps airflow and looks tidy. | Use zip ties, cut excess cable lengths. |
|15 | **Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or missing power. | Double‑check all screws, cables, and that no metal contacts the case. |
|16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, secure screws. |
|17 | **First Power‑On** | Verify hardware works. | Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse, power cable. Press power button. |
|18 | **Enter BIOS/UEFI** | Configure boot order, check temperatures. | Press key (Del/F2) during boot. |
|19 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows, Linux, etc. |
|20 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware functions correctly. | Download motherboard chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi drivers. |
|21 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, etc.). |

---

## Detailed Tips & Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Static Damage** | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or touch a grounded metal object before handling components. |
| **CPU Overheating** | Ensure the cooler is properly seated; use enough thermal paste. |
| **Poor Airflow** | Position intake fans at the front, exhaust at the rear/top. Keep cables out of the airflow path. |
| **Wrong PSU Wattage** | Use a PSU calculator; add ~20% headroom for future upgrades. |
| **BIOS Not Detecting GPU** | Make sure the GPU is fully seated and power connectors are attached. |
| **No Boot** | Check that the motherboard is correctly mounted on standoffs; no metal contact with case. |
| **Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)** | Verify RAM is seated; run memory diagnostics. |

---

## Quick Reference: Common Component Compatibility

| Component | Key Compatibility Checks |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| **Motherboard** | CPU socket, RAM type (DDR4/DDR5), form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX). |
| **CPU** | Socket type, chipset support, TDP (thermal design power). |
| **RAM** | Speed supported by motherboard, dual‑channel vs single. |
| **GPU** | PCIe slot version, power connectors, case clearance. |
| **PSU** | Wattage, connector types (24‑pin, 8‑pin EPS, PCIe). |
| **Case** | Form factor, drive bay size, cooling options. |

---

## Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner, price comparison, compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help and troubleshooting.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals for specific instructions.

---

### Final Checklist Before First Boot

- [ ] All screws tightened (motherboard, PSU, GPU, drives).  
- [ ] All cables connected (24‑pin, 8‑pin EPS, PCIe, SATA).  
- [ ] No loose tools or metal objects inside the case.  
- [ ] Monitor, keyboard, mouse connected.  
- [ ] Power cable plugged in.  

Once you hit power, you should see the BIOS screen. From there, you can set up your OS and enjoy your brand‑new PC! Happy building!
